verdict: STELLAR ACTIVITY. 69% of the classified dim variables fall in rotational, solar-like, young-stellar, eclipsing or long-period classes -- all of which dim the optical relative to the infrared through cool starspots or circumstellar material. Spots in particular predict the inversion that defeated the averaging explanation: coverage sets the mean deficit while only the asymmetric part of the spot distribution modulates, so a heavily spotted star is strongly dimmed and barely variable.
